brief.topic: Optimizing llama.cpp performance with multiple GPUs
brief.problem_or_goal: Discussing methods to improve token generation speed in llama.cpp when using multiple GPUs, particularly with mixed hardware.
brief.context: This discussion is based on an archived user account from May 7, 2025, detailing their experiments with llama.cpp on a system with a 3090 and two 3060 GPUs. The original author explored tensor splitting and row split modes to enhance performance with various models.
brief.motivation: Understanding how to configure tensor splitting and other settings in llama.cpp can significantly impact performance when running large language models on multi-GPU setups. This question aims to explore these techniques based on the archived observations.
brief.desired_response: A discussion about the effectiveness of tensor splitting and row split modes in llama.cpp for optimizing performance on multi-GPU systems, referencing the observations made in the source material.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: For smaller models like Qwen3 8B and Qwen3 14B, disabling the 3060 GPUs resulted in a performance boost.
facts.evidence_quote: If we disable them, we see a performance boost: from 48 to 82 tokens per second, and from 28 to 48.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For Qwen3 32B, adjusting the tensor split improved performance from 13.0 to 15.6 tokens per second, and further to 16.4 tokens per second using the "row" split mode.
facts.evidence_quote: We can improve performance from the default 13.0 tokens per second to 15.6 by adjusting the tensor split. Furthermore, we can go even higher, to 16.4 tokens per second, by using the "row" split mode.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For Nemotron 49B (Q6), tuning resulted in an improvement from 12.4 to 14.1 tokens per second.
facts.evidence_quote: With some tuning, we can go from 12.4 to 14.1 tokens per second.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B (Q4), performance improved from 10.3 to 12.1 tokens per second.
facts.evidence_quote: We start at 10.3 tokens per second and improve to 12.1.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For Gemma3 27B, optimized tensor split values boosted performance from 14.9 to 18.9 tokens per second, but using `sm` row mode slightly decreased speed to 18.5.
facts.evidence_quote: With optimized tensor split values, we boost performance from 14.9 to 18.9 tokens per second. However, using `sm` row mode slightly decreases the speed to 18.5.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For Mistral Small 24B, performance increased from 18.8 to 28.2 tokens per second with tensor split, but `sm` row mode reduced it slightly to 26.1.
facts.evidence_quote: Performance goes from 18.8 to 28.2 tokens per second with tensor split, but again, `sm` row mode reduces it slightly to 26.1.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

allowed_claims: Tensor splitting can be used to manage model VRAM requirements across multiple GPUs.
Different split modes ('row', 'sm') may yield varying performance results.
Experimentation is key to finding optimal tensor split configurations for specific models and hardware.
forbidden_claims: The reported token-per-second values are universally applicable.
The 'row' split mode is always superior.
Specific hardware configurations are guaranteed to achieve these exact results.
